solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: High-flier bans security, cutting back

indicators.note: back tells us the run of letters taken from those words is read in reverse
the answer cuts across the two words bans and security, sitting inside them

explanation.surface: An airline tightens its security budget, cutting back on safety measures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' picks out ANSSEC from bANS SECurity, and 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cessna is a well-known make of light aircraft, so a playful 'high-flier'.

clue.text: Heavy-footed Gaelic man leaves a party unfulfilled

indicators.note: leaves says that the single letter a departs from the name before it

parts.note: Calum is a Scottish Gaelic boy's name

indicators.note: unfulfilled means the word party is emptied, keeping only its outer letters

explanation.surface: A Scotsman stomps out of a disappointing party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves a' takes the A out of CALUM, giving CLUM; 'unfulfilled' leaves just P and Y of party.
explanation.definitionFit: Clumpy walking is heavy and clumsy, the tread of someone heavy-footed.

clue.text: Maritime craft, self-contained, limits fruit

parts.note: SC is the property-advert abbreviation for a self-contained flat
rims are edges or limits
a haw is the red fruit of the hawthorn

explanation.surface: A self-sufficient sea craft carries fruit within its bounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maritime craft' suggests a boat, but it is a craft in the sense of a handicraft practised by sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrimshaw is the carving of designs on whalebone and teeth, a traditional art of seafarers.

clue.text: On jetty, leg turned comparatively cold

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places the first piece above the jetty word
turned means the word for leg is read backwards

parts.note: pin is slang for a leg
a pier is a jetty

explanation.surface: Someone on a pier twists a leg in the chilly weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Nippy weather is chilly, so the comparative form means colder.

clue.text: Between you and me, trap is rigged somewhere in house?

indicators.note: Between says the rearranged letters go between the letters of the word for you and me

parts.note: us means you and me

indicators.note: rigged means set up or fixed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A confidential aside: the trap has been set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Between you and me' reads as a confidential aside, but it is the container of the scrambled letters; 'rigged' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Upstairs is a location within a house, on an upper floor.

clue.text: Right to split ginger, chopping food?

indicators.note: to split means the letter for right breaks into the word for ginger

parts.note: pep, like ginger, means energy or vim

explanation.surface: Fresh ginger is ready for dicing in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: Prep is kitchen shorthand for preparation, the chopping done before cooking.

clue.text: Head to the outskirts to evade explosion — one might enter a bunker

indicators.note: Head asks for the first letter of the word the
outskirts asks for only the outer letters of the word evade

parts.note: a shot is a blast or explosion

explanation.surface: Someone heads out of town to escape a bomb blast and takes refuge in a bunker.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'to's are link words: 'Head to the' gives T, 'outskirts to evade' gives EE. A golf bunker is a sand trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A golfer's drive from the tee can land in a sand bunker if mishit.

clue.text: Dragon perhaps mentioned in folk legend

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, so the phrase is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: in lore: lore is folk legend

explanation.surface: A dragon appears in a folk tale.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is the dreaded mother-in-law cast as a dragon; in a non-rhotic British accent the phrase sounds exactly like it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fearsome relation by marriage, such as a mother-in-law, is jokingly called a dragon.

clue.text: Half of Surrey players initially go up to bowl over

indicators.note: Half of keeps only the first three of the six letters of the county name
initially keeps only the opening letter of players, dropping everything after it

parts.note: to rise is to go up

explanation.surface: Half the Surrey cricket team come up to bowl. Surrey is an English county with a cricket side.
explanation.definitionFit: To bowl someone over is to astonish them, to take them by surprise.

clue.text: Gravestone might display this in a French green

indicators.note: in places the gravestone letters inside the French word

parts.note: une is French for a
RIP, rest in peace, is carved on gravestones

explanation.surface: A headstone in France stands in a grassy plot.
explanation.definitionFit: Green fruit is not yet ripe, so green means immature here.

clue.text: Party animal passed over bar a drug in each hand

indicators.note: passed over means the word for bar is turned back over itself

parts.note: a lever is a bar

indicators.note: in puts the drug letter between the two hands

parts.note: L and R stand for left and right hands
E is the slang abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A clubber walks past the bar holding a pill in each hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A reveller is someone who parties hard, a party animal.

clue.text: Fatty food nut gobbles M&M — heading for illness?

indicators.note: gobbles means the nut word swallows the other letters

parts.note: a pecan is a nut
the two Ms taken as written

indicators.note: heading for asks for the first letter of illness

explanation.surface: Someone scoffing nuts and M&Ms is heading for illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Pemmican is a dried meat and fat mixture, a traditional high-energy ration.

clue.text: Turns away non-Democrat promotions

indicators.note: non signals that the Democrat letter is absent from the word

parts.note: adverts are promotions

explanation.surface: A Republican refuses promotions offered to non-Democrats.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert something is to turn it aside, as in averting one's eyes.

clue.text: Demonstrate to 'elen a bathroom feature?

parts.note: to show is to demonstrate
Helen with her H dropped, as in a Cockney voice: show 'er, show her

explanation.surface: A Cockney shows Helen round the new bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: Demonstrate to her is show her; drop the H, as the clue does to 'elen, and you have SHOW 'ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A shower is a fixture for washing, found in most bathrooms.

clue.text: Roman number used during visit by accountant

indicators.note: used during puts the number letter inside the word for visit

parts.note: to see someone is to visit them
CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: An accountant crunches a number on a visit.
explanation.definitionFit: Seneca was a Roman philosopher and statesman, so a Roman by example.

clue.text: Nag spouse latterly during dad's 1930s film

parts.note: a nag is a horse

indicators.note: during puts the last letter of spouse inside the dad word

parts.note: dad's gives the father's, here written as fathers

indicators.note: latterly asks for the final letter of spouse

explanation.surface: A wife nags her husband through Dad's favourite old movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse Feathers is a 1932 Marx Brothers comedy.

clue.text: Quivering tree put everyone in a state all the time

indicators.note: quivering means shaking about, so the letters of tree are jumbled
in puts the word for everyone inside the state letters

parts.note: NY is New York, a US state
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A tree trembles as everyone gets worked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternally means forever, without end, so constantly.

clue.text: Neighbouring worker keeps record-player in top condition

indicators.note: keeps means the worker word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: an ant is the usual crossword worker
a DJ plays records
ace means excellent, first-rate

explanation.surface: A worker keeps an old gramophone well maintained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record-player' suggests a turntable, but it is a disc jockey.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjacent means lying next to, so neighbouring.

clue.text: Where Lancashire river anglers go, we hear, until the match's final stages?

indicators.note: we hear signals that the phrase is replaced by one sounding the same

parts.note: the Wyre is a river in Lancashire, a county in north-west England, so anglers go down to the Wyre

explanation.surface: Fishermen head off to a Lancashire river as a match nears its end.
explanation.definitionFit: A contest that goes down to the wire stays undecided until its last moments, an idiom from horse racing.

clue.text: Nervous habits stifling performance — the subject of pre-match talk?

indicators.note: stifling means the habits word smothers the performance word inside it

parts.note: tics are nervous twitches
an act is a performance

explanation.surface: A player's nervous twitches spoil his performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Team talks before a game set out strategy and how to play.

clue.text: Excessively treat Asian runner, removing toe (large)

indicators.note: in a down clue the toe is the bottom letter, so the last letter of the river goes

parts.note: the Indus is a major river of Pakistan; a river runs
LGE is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: An Asian athlete lost a toe, and it was a large one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' is a river, not an athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: To indulge someone is to spoil them with too many treats.

clue.text: White Swan's old comedian Jack welcomes non-boozer

indicators.note: welcomes means the comedian's name takes the other letters in

parts.note: Jack Dee is a British stand-up comedian
TT means teetotal

explanation.surface: An old comic lets a teetotaller into the White Swan pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White Swan' looks like a pub name, but it is the ballet role.
explanation.definitionFit: Odette is the white swan princess in Tchaikovsky's Swan Lake.

clue.text: Junkie confronted prosecutor, policeman and court

indicators.note: confronted, read as con-fronted, turns the prosecutor letters back to front

parts.note: DA is a US district attorney
DI is a detective inspector

explanation.surface: A drug user faces the prosecutor, the police and the court.
explanation.definitionFit: An addict is someone dependent on drugs, a junkie.

clue.text: Some plumbing finally added before shower installed

indicators.note: before places the letter ahead of the shower word
finally asks for the last letter of added

parts.note: rain is a shower

explanation.surface: A plumber finishes the job by installing a shower.
explanation.definitionFit: A drain is a pipe carrying away waste water, part of a house's plumbing.

clue.text: Set hour with A Study in Scarlet

indicators.note: in puts the study word inside the colour

parts.note: scarlet is a shade of red
a den is a study

explanation.surface: Someone sits down for an hour with the Sherlock Holmes novel A Study in Scarlet.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sherlock Holmes title is not a unit: 'in' is a container signal, putting the study inside the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardened and set both describe something that has become solid, like concrete.

clue.text: Typical movement by 21, lowest class, beneath aeroplane

indicators.note: in a down clue, beneath puts the class letter below the aeroplane word

parts.note: a jet is an aeroplane
E is the lowest grade or class

explanation.surface: A ballerina in economy class flies below in a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 refers to ODETTE, a ballet role, so the movement is a ballet step.
explanation.definitionFit: A jete is a ballet leap, the kind of step Odette dances.

clue.text: One inspects digger after fire's repelled

indicators.note: after places the digger word following the other piece
repelled means driven back, so the word for fire is reversed

parts.note: to axe someone is to fire them; the 's is is
a miner digs

explanation.surface: An inspector checks a miner after an underground fire is beaten back.
explanation.definitionFit: An examiner is a person who inspects or tests.

clue.text: Dim one left cashbox on counter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: on counter is read as running counter, against the direction, so the word for cashbox is reversed

parts.note: a till is a cashbox

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper leaves the cash box on the counter in the gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on counter' suggests a shop counter, but means going the opposite way.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-lit means poorly lighted, so dim.

clue.text: In retrospect, Web surfing, in extreme cases, attracts fanatic element

indicators.note: In retrospect means looking back, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: the Net is the internet, the Web

indicators.note: in extreme cases asks for only the outer letters of surfing

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast or fanatic

explanation.surface: A web-surfing obsessive draws in fanatics.
explanation.definitionFit: Tungsten is a chemical element, a hard grey metal.

clue.text: Press buttons again? This closes your car

indicators.note: This closes points to the closing letter of the word your

parts.note: the E-Type is a classic Jaguar sports car

explanation.surface: Pressing the button again shuts your car.
explanation.definitionFit: To retype is to key text in once more, pressing the keys a second time.
